newsitem.title: ITALY: Committal hearing for Italy's Prodi adjourned.
newsitem.headline: Committal hearing for Italy's Prodi adjourned.

text.p: A committal hearing that must decide whether Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi should be tried for alleged abuse of office and conflict of interest was adjourned until February 28 when it formally opened on Wednesday.

The decision to adjourn, taken behind closed doors, was announced to reporters by Prodi's lawyer Paola Severino. Prodi denies the allegations, which relate to a controversial sale by state holding company IRI when he was chairman in 1993.

Prosecutor Giuseppa Geremia alleges that Prodi and five other IRI board members at the time awarded an "unjust advantage" to a little-known southern Italian consortium, Fis.Vi., in its purchase of food company Cirio.

Presiding judge Edoardo Landi took just 40 minutes to decide on the adjournment. It was conceded at the request of a defence lawyer who was engaged on Wednesday at another trial in Turin, northern Italy.
Prodi did not attend the hearing and only one of the defendants was present for the brief session.

"We were ready to discuss our aspects of the case as of today but the reasons for a delay were well-founded. February 28 was the date all lawyers were available so we will continue then," Severino said.
